name: Experience Coffin Bay
summary: Boat tours of the Coffin Bay oyster farms from the Coffin Bay Yacht Club, run by Chris and Linda Hank, who grew oysters from 1996 before starting boat tours. The three hour Farm & Bay Tour includes an optional wade through an oyster farm in supplied waders, and dolphins and seals are often seen along the way, though not guaranteed. A shorter tour, private hire and coach group bookings are also offered.
standouts: Run by oyster growers Chris and Linda Hank, who grew oysters from 1996 before starting boat tours
Quoted on the site as the number 1 thing to do in Coffin Bay on Trip Advisor
Winner, SA Life Magazine Absolute Best, SA Tourism Experience Award (as stated on the site)
2026 Hello SA Top Tour Guide (as stated on the site)

contact.address: Coffin Bay Yacht Club, 146 Esplanade, Coffin Bay SA 5607 (Berth 5)

trips.title: Farm & Bay Tour
trips.summary: A three hour boat tour from the Coffin Bay Yacht Club to a prime growing oyster farm, past secluded islands, beaches and the Coffin Bay National Park coastline. At the farm, guests can wade through the oyster beds in supplied waders or stay on the boat, and one dozen freshly shucked oysters are included. Dolphins and seals are often seen, though not guaranteed.
highlights: Optional wading through an oyster farm in supplied waders
One dozen freshly shucked oysters included
Brothers Island, a known sea lion and seal spot, is explored on this tour
Local beer, wine and Coffin Bay gin to buy on board
trips.departsFrom: Coffin Bay Yacht Club Floating Marina, Berth 5, Coffin Bay
includes: One dozen freshly shucked oysters per paying passenger, served natural with fresh lemon
Waders supplied for the wading experience
Wasabi and Tabasco sauce to have with the oysters
bring: Hat, sunglasses, sunscreen and a warm jacket in case the wind comes up
In warmer months, bathers or shorts you are happy to get wet; wetsuit boots or water shoes if not wearing waders
trips.requirements: Check in 20 minutes before departure. At least 4 paying passengers are needed for the tour to run. Waders are sized by shoe size, with a small number of children's sizes; very large builds may not fit and can wear their own bathers. No dogs. Wheelchair boarding is from a floating pontoon with 800mm wide doors; the toilet is not wheelchair accessible. Booking age bands: adults 17 to 59, seniors 60 and over with a seniors card, students 17 and over with student identification, children 2 to 16. Cards are checked at check in. Children under 2 are welcome with a parent, subject to numbers, and the business asks to be told when booking.

trips.title: Short & Sweet Tour
trips.summary: A 1.5 hour boat tour from the Coffin Bay Yacht Club to an oyster farm just outside Coffin Bay township. A veteran oyster farmer hosts, sharing how premium Coffin Bay oysters are produced, teaching guests to shuck, and visiting the first oyster farm in Coffin Bay. Six freshly shucked oysters are included.
highlights: Hosted by a veteran oyster farmer
Visits the first oyster farm in Coffin Bay
Six freshly shucked oysters included; no wading on this tour

trips.title: Private Tours
trips.summary: Private hire of the tour boat for functions, corporate events, parties and special occasions, for up to 30 people. The boat is fully enclosed with bistro style seating, a toilet and a bar. Bookings are made by enquiry.
highlights: Fully enclosed boat with bistro style seating
Suited to functions, corporate events and parties
